newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open firmer.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open firmer.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were called to open firmer Tuesday as gold rebounded overnight from the lows after Monday's selloff in New York ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
COMEX June gold was called to open up $0.50 to $1.00 an ounce from Monday's close of $342.20. It traded $343.80 to $341.30 on overnight ACCESS.
Early bullion was quoted at $342.90/$343.40 an ounce, and London gold fixed at $342.50 Tuesday morning, up $1.80.
COMEX July silver was called to open up 0.50 to 1.00 cent and was traded $4.735 to $4.685 in overnight ACCESS.
The Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee (FOMC) meets Tuesday as the financial markets waited to see if there will be any change to interest rates.
COMEX gold stocks on Monday fell 1,093 ounces to 893,935 ounces, while the exchange's silver stocks rose 1,114,611 ounces to 193,273,492 ounces.
NYMEX July platinum and NYMEX June palladium were both called to open $0.50 to $1.00 an ounce firmer.
Palladium continued to strengthen on concerns over the lack of Russian supplies in the market, and fixed at $177.50 an ounce in London Tuesday, its highest since April 5, 1995.
